To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

eukaryotic translation initiation factor 3 is involved in the regulation of a subset of mRNAs that control cell growth, and that eIF3 exerts either translational activation (c-Jun) or repression (BTG1) of mRNA expression through binding to specific RNA stem–loop structures in the 5’ untranslated regions of mRNAs.

eIF3 targets a highly specific set of mRNAs that encode proteins involved in controlling cell proliferation and differentiation, and that the interaction of eIF3 with these mRNAs can either activate or repress translation.
eIF3 binds specifically to the 5′UTRs of mRNAs that encode cell cycle regulators.
